message.content:
I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, so I can’t tell you your exact download/upload speeds.  
Here’s what you can do to find out:

| Method | How to use it |
|--------|---------------|
| **Web speed‑test sites** | Visit a site such as <https://www.speedtest.net> or <https://fast.com>. Click “Go” and wait for the test to finish. |
| **Command‑line (if you have Python)** | Install the `speedtest-cli` package (`pip install speedtest-cli`) and run `speedtest-cli`. |
| **Windows PowerShell** | If you have PowerShell 7+, you can use the `Invoke-WebRequest` cmdlet to download a file from a known server and calculate the speed yourself. |

If you’d like a quick command‑line test and you’re on Windows, you can run:

```powershell
# PowerShell 7+ example
$uri = "https://speed.hetzner.de/100MB.bin"
$start = Get-Date
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $uri -OutFile "$env:TEMP\speedtest.bin"
$end = Get-Date
$bytes = (Get-Item "$env:TEMP\speedtest.bin").Length
$seconds = ($end - $start).TotalSeconds
$mbps = ($bytes / 1_000_000) / $seconds
Write-Host "Download speed: $([math]::Round($mbps,2)) MB/s"
Remove-Item "$env:TEMP\speedtest.bin"
```

Just copy that into a PowerShell window and hit Enter. It will download a 100 MB file from Hetzner’s test server and report the average download speed.

Let me know if you need help setting up any of these options!
